text:
alex: quick heads-up — apac-gpu-pool is seeing 95th latency jump from ~120ms -> 850ms starting ~10:12UTC. spike aligns with a small set of tenants doing very large batched token streams. looks like kvcache churn + proxy fallbacks. cc @maya @raja
maya: ugh okay. any trace ids or tenant ids? can we confirm fallback routing to dedicated/burst lanes?
alex: tenant id t-742 and t-801. I pulled a short sample from the trace service:
```
trace_id=tr-0a1b2c3d slot=apac-gpu-12 path=proxy->runtime fallback=true kv_miss=0.82 batch_size=128 latency_ms=860
trace_id=tr-0a1b2c4e slot=apac-gpu-17 path=proxy->runtime fallback=true kv_miss=0.79 batch_size=64 latency_ms=640
```
alex: also saw a bunch of egress queue droppings and nic tx spikes. putting logs here: https://internal.logs/redwood/apac/4850004321
raja: is this causing dedicated pool autoscaler to spin up? that would explain cost bleed. sam can you check DedicatedPool billing alerts?
sam: looking — yes, there were 3 rapid pool spin-ups 10:13-10:18 which triggered burst capacity. cost delta ~+9% for the hour. not catastrophic but noisy.
maya: probable root: these tenants do periodic large-batch streaming jobs (LLM scoring). kv cache regen at that batch size kills prefix hits and trips fallback routing which spreads load across more GPUs. solution ideas: 1) soft-quarantine/slow-path for arms-length tenants 2) prewarming for detected batch patterns 3) per-tenant batch caps or shaping at proxy
liu: +1 on shaping. we can quick-probe a proxy rate cap per-tenant for batch_size>64 and >QPS threshold. low-risk toggle behind feature flag.
alex: can we run a canary for shaping in apac-edge only? don't want to impact their latency SLAs for small requests. suggest 1% of t-742 traffic first.
raja: ops-bot — create canary ticket and add to weekly roll plan, tag: isolation-shaping-apac
ops-bot: ticket created: ISOL-APAC-4321 by raja — canary shaping 1% -> 10% -> 100% rollout steps. assigned to eng-infra and runtime. ETA staging test 2h. :white_check_mark:
sam: also propose adding a cost guard: if dedicated pool scale-up within 5m and triggered by <5 tenants, block auto-burst and notify oncall before provisioning (opt-in flag).
maya: agree, we'll need fallback safety so we don't cause customer-facing failures. implement a temporary soft-quarantine that redirects suspicious batches to preemptible fractional slices first.
liu: config snippet for quick test (proxy):
```
# proxy config override (canary)
rules:
  - match: tenant == "t-742" and batch_size > 64 and qps > 1
    action: shape
    params: {max_batch: 64, rate_limit: 10r/s, canary_pct: 1}
```
liu: will push to staging in 30m.
alex: excellent. after canary, we'll monitor kv_miss, fallback rate, dedicated-pool spinups, and 95th latency. set alerts: fallback_rate > 5% and dedicated_spinups > 2 in 10m.
raja: also add a small telemetry label so we can attribute cost-blips to the shaping rule: telemetry.tag=isolation_canary_v1
sam: FYI we'll also run a retrospective on t-742's usage pattern — maybe reach out to tenant owners to recommend optimal batching or a dedicated reserved pool if they need this throughput.
maya: sounds good. schedule a short ops sync in 1h to review canary metrics. :calendar:
alex: thanks all. i'll post a short runbook for rollback if errors spike.
liu: pushed staging config and test traffic started. trace ids will start tr-0a1b2c9x in ~5m.
ops-bot: canary monitor created in grafana: dashboard ISOLATION-CANARY-APAC-4850004321
alex: leaving this thread pinned to eng-infra for updates. simple messages only pls — no long essays. :hand:
maya: update in 18m: initial 1% canary reduced fallback rate for t-742 from 18% -> 6% and 95th latency for apac pool dropped to ~220ms. continuing ramp.
raja: nice. keep rollout plan ready, but let's gate full rollout on cost guard and oncall ack.
sam: noted — cost guard PR incoming.
alex: closing loop: if canary keeps improving metrics we'll promote to 10% -> 50% over next 6h. thanks everyone.
